free_tier.stated: Free Basic plan (since 2025-05-29): 5 published documents max, each capped at 50 MB and 10 pages.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Reader-facing views are free and CDN-served, but documents beyond the 5 allowance stay hosted yet become "inaccessible to readers". So serving capacity is not proportional to stored bytes.

tooling: Issuu API v2 exists (OAuth, upload/publish endpoints) with an official SDK github.com/issuu/issuu-api-sdk; API v1 is deprecated in favour of v2. API access does not lift the free-plan document caps.
chaining: 5 documents x 50 MB = 250 MB per account at best; unlimited accounts gives 250 MB units. Hopeless next to 10 TiB.
limits_note: 5 published docs; 50 MB per document; 10 pages per document; only the 5 most recent remain publicly readable; cannot choose which 5.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Documents over the allowance are silently made unreadable (still stored, retrievable only by the logged-in publisher), so public serving breaks without any error.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

evidence.proved: 'Free Basic users are now limited to 5 published documents, with each document restricted to a maximum of 50MB in size and 10 pages'
downgrade behaviour, publications stay hosted but unreadable
